text: I see you have right leg weakness, an unsteady gait, multiple falls, forgetfulness, and paranoid behavior. To determine the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your vision, such as double vision or loss of vision in one eye?

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your recent onset of leg weakness and falls alongside memory loss and personality changes, did you notice any sudden confusion, slurred speech, or severe headache when these symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Right leg weakness and unsteady gait. I also have Forgetfulness, Paranoid and agitated behavior, Difficulty in using kitchen appliances.

speaker: Doctor
text: The unsteady gait, right leg weakness, and falls suggest a spinal cord or brainstem issue. Given the 6-month history of forgetfulness and paranoia, could you describe any changes in your bladder or bowel control, such as incontinence or difficulty holding your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known history of HIV, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Noncompliance with medications for over 2 years. Social history: Information not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: HIV-associated vacuolar myelopathy with opportunistic CNS infection (e.g., Toxoplasmosis or Cryptococcus).
